Last year, the amount of money spent on lobbying hit a record $5.24 billion dollars at the federal level alone… and well… I don’t know if you realized, but there weren't even any major federal elections in 2025. 
When you factor in the upcoming midterms, state and local level lobbying in addition to all of the money spent outside of officially disclosed channels, the volume of cash that is… uhh “enabling” the law making process is going to eclipse 11 figures within America alone this year… and by all accounts it’s going to be a great investment… 
A cambridge university report found that out of 1,779 policy issues passed during their study, the preferences of economic elites and special business interests had a significant influence on policy outcomes which wasn’t really the shocking part… 
The shocking part was that the preferences of average citizens had effectively no measurable influence, even in large groups that were extremely politically active. Oh and this study was done in 2014, when total political spending was less than a quarter of what it is today… 
Part of the reason WHY that spending has become so ludicrous is not because the money is being used to circumvent the will of the people, (that battle was won long ago), it’s instead become a spending battle between OTHER lobbyists to see whose special interests take precedence over the lessor donors… 
but even if we somehow reformed this in its entirety tomorrow, we only need to look to other countries to see that it’s probably not going to fix all of our problems… 
Oh and of course… this is all assuming that everybody was actually playing by those rules in the first place…

Many countries have looked to Singapore’s public housing model, where homes are sold on 99-year leases, as a way to improve affordability, but can it be replicated in places where governments do not control most of the land?

Click here to subscribe to our channel 👉🏽 https://bbc.in/3VyyriM

Australia is scaling back tax incentives for property investors in an effort to improve housing affordability, but whether the reforms will meaningfully lower home prices remains an open question. 

In this episode, Mariko Oi speaks with Bill Birtles and Abhiram Subramaniam about Australia's housing changes, the affordability crisis across Asia, and what countries such as South Korea, China and Singapore can teach us about tackling soaring housing costs.

snippet.title: Tracking Suspected Members of the Pakistani Taliban | Taliban Hunters (full documentary) | FRONTLINE
snippet.description:
Inside a counterterrorism police unit in Karachi, Pakistan, dedicated to tracking down suspected members of the Pakistani Taliban. (Aired 2015)

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

In the nearly five years since the Taliban seized control of Afghanistan, there’s been a dramatic increase in attacks within neighboring Pakistan by the militant group Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan, commonly called the Pakistani Taliban or TTP. Pakistan has accused Taliban-controlled Afghanistan of harboring the group and enabling it to launch cross-border attacks, which the Afghan government denies — and in recent weeks, the fight between the two countries escalated into what Pakistan’s government called “open war.”

Against this volatile backdrop, FRONTLINE’s 2015 documentary “Taliban Hunters” offers relevant history on TTP and Pakistani security forces’ fight against it. This short documentary went inside a Karachi-based counterterrorism police unit dedicated to tracking down Taliban suspects. 

As the documentary reported, TTP first emerged in 2007 and used to have only a small, underground presence in Karachi, Pakistan’s largest city. But by the time the documentary aired, the group had been gaining ground in the city of over 20 million people, and carrying out suicide bombings and targeted assassinations there.

The film documented how the unit carried out raids to take suspected TTP members into custody. It also explored human rights groups’ allegations that Karachi authorities were abusing militants captured in the city’s fight against terrorism. Amid TTP’s current resurgence, “Taliban Hunters” is an illuminating snapshot of where the fight against them stood in one large city back in 2015, and how the group operated.

“Taliban Hunters” is directed and reported by Mobeen Azhar and produced by Jamie Doran. The senior producer for FRONTLINE is Dan Edge.

Amidst all of the chaos of last week, the world's largest asset manager (blackrock) quietly announced something that should be making a lot of people extremely worried. 
They would be limiting withdrawals on one of their flagship private credit funds that currently has (or at least had) 26 billion dollars worth of assets under management. 
Now I know that there is a lot going on in the world right now and compared to some of the headlines we have seen in the past week this might sound pretty minor, but a hiccup like this in these markets could genuinely be the sign, symptom and cause of something much scarier. 
On one hand, people pulling money out of these kinds of funds is a sign that things are not going well amongst even the most high end investors. 
On the other hand, the fact that they can’t get their money out is a symptom of people predicting things are about to get much worse… 
And on the third hand, a shocking amount of everyday businesses have been propped up by the easy lending done by firms like this… If their money stops flowing, it could easily cause much larger knock on effects throughout the real economy in extremely direct ways. 
But before we get too hyperbolic, it’s important to understand exactly what these funds were supposed to do and more importantly what they have actually been doing, because depending on your interpretation of this business model, this headline is either little more than dumb investors not understanding what they invested in… or it’s the modern equivalent of a bank run. 
The total debt outstanding in this highly risky class of finance is now over 2 trillion dollars (and that’s only what we actually know of), either way that’s almost twice as much as the 1.3 trillion dollars in subprime mortgage lending done in 2008, and with an alarming number of parallels it’s clear to see why some people are getting nervous… 
Now that alone is… not great… but it gets worse…
If one Blackrock fund really was the only fund having problems it could probably just be written off as (a concerning but ultimately) isolated incident, unfortunately though, this week's announcement was just the latest (and so far) largest example of major issues in these multi trillion dollar private markets…

snippet.title: Space Economy Reality Check: SpaceX at $1.77 Trillion
snippet.description:
SpaceX’s 1.77 trillion dollar IPO valuation is not just a story about rockets. It is a story about power, infrastructure, satellite internet, defense, artificial intelligence, and the future of the global space economy.

In this video, we break down why investors are pricing SpaceX like one of the most important companies in the world, even though the company is still spending heavily on Starship, Starlink, AI infrastructure, and future space systems. The big question is simple: is SpaceX really worth 1.77 trillion dollars, or is Wall Street buying a dream before the business model has fully arrived?

We explain how SpaceX became more than a launch company. Falcon 9 gave it dominance in reusable rockets. Starlink turned orbit into a subscription internet business. Starship could change the economics of moving mass into space. And government demand, especially from defense and national security, could make SpaceX one of the most strategically important companies in the world.

But the space economy is often misunderstood. Most of the real money today is not in Mars colonies or asteroid mining. It is in satellite communications, GPS, Earth observation, military networks, launch services, ground terminals, aviation internet, maritime connectivity, and remote broadband. Space is valuable because Earth already depends on it.

This video also looks at the geopolitical side of SpaceX. What happens when one private company controls critical space infrastructure? What does it mean for the United States, China, Europe, Russia, and developing countries? Could Starlink become a global communications layer? Could SpaceX become the railroad, telecom network, and military logistics provider of the orbital economy?

The SpaceX IPO is not just a financial event. It may be the moment public markets started treating space as the next major infrastructure layer of the global economy.

Watch until the end for the full breakdown of the SpaceX valuation, the real space economy, the Starlink business model, the Starship risk, and the geopolitical battle for control of orbit.

snippet.title: Venezuela earthquake: How long can trapped victims survive under rubble? - BBC World Service

Click here to subscribe to our channel 👉🏽 https://bbc.in/3VyyriM

But there is a lack of heavy machinery and specialised equipment needed to rescue people. Much of the emergency response is being carried out by volunteers and international aid workers from Turkey, the UK and France. BBC’s Global Affairs reporter Mimi Swaby gives us the latest update on the situation.

Against all odds, several videos online show miraculous stories of survival, like young infants and children being lifted from the rubble. snippet.title: Honda Just Lost Money for the First Time Since the 1950s
snippet.description:
Honda was supposed to be one of the safest names in the automotive industry. For decades, the Japanese giant survived oil shocks, economic recessions, financial crises, and fierce global competition while maintaining an extraordinary record of profitability. Yet in 2026, that streak came to an end. Honda reported its first annual loss since becoming a publicly traded company in the 1950s, sending shockwaves through the automotive and investment worlds.

What happened? How did one of the most respected manufacturers on Earth go from engineering excellence to a historic financial loss?

In this video, we break down the real story behind Honda’s multi billion dollar setback. We examine how the global electric vehicle boom encouraged automakers to invest massive sums into battery plants, EV factories, and ambitious electrification strategies. We explore why many executives believed EV adoption would accelerate much faster than it actually did, and how slowing demand, changing government incentives, rising interest rates, and intense competition from Chinese manufacturers created a perfect storm for legacy automakers.

You will learn why Honda was forced to suspend major EV projects, write down billions of dollars in investments, and rethink its long term strategy. We also examine the surprising role that Honda’s motorcycle division played in helping stabilize the company during one of the most challenging periods in its modern history.

But this story is about more than Honda. It reveals a much larger shift happening across the global automotive industry. Companies that once promised an all electric future are increasingly turning back toward hybrid vehicles. Investors are questioning whether the EV transition will happen as quickly as predicted. Governments, manufacturers, battery suppliers, and energy companies are all being forced to adjust expectations.

Is Honda simply the first major casualty of an overhyped EV boom? Or is this a temporary setback that will ultimately make the company stronger? More importantly, what does Honda’s historic loss tell us about the future of transportation, manufacturing, technology, and the global economy?

From boardroom decisions and billion dollar investments to geopolitical competition and changing consumer behavior, this documentary explores one of the most important business stories of the year. If you want to understand where the automotive industry is heading next, and why some of the biggest companies in the world are changing course, this is a story you cannot afford to miss.

Watch until the end to discover why Honda’s first major loss in generations may not be the end of an era, but the beginning of a completely different automotive future.

snippet.description:
What if the future of global food security depends on a resource most people have never heard of?

When discussions turn to critical resources, attention usually focuses on oil, natural gas, lithium, semiconductors, or rare earth minerals. Yet there is another resource that may be even more essential to human civilization. I mean… I don’t know about you guys. After the age of thirty I personally have like three and a half friends in total and even keeping up with them takes some time management…
All of this is especially eye opening when you additionally consider that he didn’t exactly have a flawless reputation to begin with. 
These were supposedly some of the busiest most time poor individuals on the planet, and yet they all seemed to have endless availability  for social gatherings where “occasionally” Epstein may have been present… so the story goes…

The answer may seem pretty obvious, it’s a great big club and you aint in it… but what kind of club was this exactly, and has it actually stopped operating?
Oh and I guess once we have gone through all of that… I should probably address the elephant in the room… yes I was named in the Epstein files… but more on that later…

snippet.title: 'THEY LIED ABOUT TRUMP'
snippet.description:
I've been waiting 10 years to ask someone these questions, and today I finally get to do that.

Ever since I was a kid, I’ve been fascinated by American politics. Back then, I used to watch the elections, every interview and all the debates from my bedroom, trying to figure out why a system thousands of miles away felt so consequential to my life.

So when I was given the chance to have a sit-down conversation with Vice President Of The United States JD Vance, I knew I didn’t just want to ask him about headlines.

I wanted to understand the person behind the headlines.

At the start of the conversation, I said to him: “To understand the people that are sitting in front of me, you have to get a picture of their early context.”

And the reality is, I didn't truly know his context…

What I really wanted to find out by speaking with VP is: How much of what people think they know about VP Vance is ACTUALLY true?

Long before he entered the White House, VP grew up in a home shaped by addiction, poverty, instability, and a revolving door of father figures.

I went into this conversation wanting to understand how a kid raised in addiction and instability became the Vice President of the United States. And then get to the bottom of what he really thinks about everything happening in the world right now with no questions left unsaid.

We spoke about:

- The childhood instability that shaped the way he sees people.
- The conversation that changed his view of Donald Trump.
- His return to Christianity after years as an atheist.
- Whether he wants to be President one day.
- The immigration debate that is dividing America.
- Why doesn't he trust the UK Government?
- Whether he thinks aliens exist…
- When will a proposed ceasefire deal with Iran happen?
- Navigating one of the most demanding jobs on earth while raising a young family.

One of the things that I've come to learn is just try and meet everybody as I experience them.

Regardless of where you stand politically, this conversation goes deeper than politics.

And as a podcaster, having these conversations is important, as it goes beyond the headlines and shows you how the people in power actually think.

For as long as most of you have been alive, we have been told that federal debt is a major crisis just waiting to happen. 
For more than a quarter of a century at this point we have become very well acquainted with images of this debt clock, and the increasingly regular government shutdowns where they play hot potato with this ballooning hand grenade. 
If all of that wasn’t annoying enough there is almost the uniform flip flop between politicians taking turns to be very concerned about “fiscal responsibility” depending on if they are in or out of power at that time. 
t’s a powerful message… but they do seem to forget about it pretty quickly once they are in office and fixing it would require actual sacrifice, and if we are being honest with ourselves, it’s almost easy to see where this indifference is coming from. 
We were told we were at an inflection point when we crossed 10 trillion dollars in debt, and then 20 trillion, and now we are approaching 40 trillion dollars in total debt or 130% of our GDP…
The rate in which we are taking on new debt is also accelerating, almost half of all of our outstanding borrowing has been done in just the last 6 years… and yet… on the surface, you would be forgiven for thinking… not much has changed… 
And I don’t just mean that in the sense of “why haven’t we turned into Greece yet?” because this also raises a more important question… the government has spent 15 trillion dollars more than it has brought in through taxes in just the last half decade alone… so why don’t we “feel” 15 trillion dollars richer?
When will this debt, actually become a problem?

Big technology companies naturally want to stretch the limits of what they are allowed to do within the confines of the law, but effective regulators are supposed to keep them within these “guidelines”...
The only problem is that there is much much more money to be made on the other side of the technical word of the law so over time they have developed a foolproof system for getting around these “legal suggestions” to access markets that nobody else thought was possible. 
Uber got around taxi regulations, food delivery apps - minimum wage laws, buy now pay later services and consumer lending standards, AirBNB got around hotel licensing and zoning laws, crowdfunding - investment standards, and then there are even more obvious examples like “bet on everything” platforms that have skirted gambling regulations (not to mention age limits) based on extremely flimsy financial “technicalities”...
This isn’t even touching on the absolute dumpster fire that has been allowed in the grey areas of crypto currency… but the thing is, every single one of these companies that “bravely chose to venture where the law said they couldn’t” are all worth billions of dollars today… 
In the battle between technology and the law… technology is winning every… single… time… 
In the short term there are actually some genuine benefits to workers and consumers by breaking down rigid structures. But if they were willing to bend the rules in our favor to get us on board in the first place, it sets a pretty bad precedent once they have captured a market… which is exactly what we are seeing today…
Now the solution is; effective, well funded, and well staffed regulators to make sure that these businesses are abiding by the word of the law from day one… but c'mon, let’s be honest with ourselves… we all know that’s not happening any time soon…

Earlier this week the president announced on truth social that there had been productive talks with Iran to de-escalate the situation in the region, which inferred a loosening of shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, which in turn meant the potential for lower oil prices and a more positive outlook for financial markets. 
Now putting to the side for a second that these “productive talks” may or may not have happened at all, what actually got people's attention was that just 16 minutes before this announcement there was a huge spike in futures trading within these markets, clearly suggesting that someone on the inside knew what was about to happen and was profiting off it. 
Depending on the details of the trades this mystery speculator could have made as much as 60 million dollars within the span of 20 minutes… but perhaps this isn’t surprising to you anymore… 
Insider trading has effectively become the expectation in Washington at this point as everyone from senior elected officials all the way down to junior public servants consistently outperform the top hedge funds on the planet… it’s not great, but… well… people have just become numb to it, these days it’s barely worth reporting on…
It’s obviously immoral at best and borderline treasonous at worst, but at this point we know nothing is going to be done about it, and with everything else going on it is easy to assume that in the grand scheme of things this isn’t actually hurting us individually as much as everything else in the economy at the moment. 
Most people don’t really have stock investments worth worrying about and even if they did it’s hard to see the impact this kind of cheating actually has. 
This disheartening indifference is part of what makes this week's “lucky” trade in particular so interesting, people actually cared about it! And there were probably two reasons for this. 
First, it was happening in a market that was clearly hurting them right now, someone making life changing amounts of money speculating on oil prices just inherently doesn’t sit right while most people are struggling to put gas in their cars. 
The second, was simply how brazen it was.
The only reason we even know this happened at all was because (whoever they were) they made trades with hundreds of millions of dollars in notional value within the span of just 60 seconds and they did it 15 minutes before a market altering announcement. 
The point is that if this was insider trading they didn’t even have the common decency to spread their trades out over a few hours… if they did there is a good chance we would never even know… instead they are literally giving us the bird with trading volume… 
Now this particular example may be particularly infuriating, but if there is some good that may come of it, it is showing that; this happens all the time, the insiders are usually just a little bit better at hiding it.
Looking back at a few of the key changes that have enabled (what should be shameful behaviour) to become so blatant is the first step, but this itself also raises some much more important questions, like well… How much money has actually been made off political insider trading? And more importantly, how much is all of this actually costing you?!
